metadataReview.note: Fryxell's history of Charles XII states that Stuart chose the land of Toberup (also written Tiberup) north of Humlebæk, between Helsingør and Copenhagen, as the landing place. Swedish troops came ashore there against Danish entrenchments on the beach. The atlas point is the gazetteer node for the village of Tibberup in Helsingør municipality, a sector reference for the landing beach on the Øresund shore just to the east. It is not a surveyed boat-landing point, a Danish battery position or the later Swedish camp. The existing Gregorian date is retained; the Swedish-calendar 25 July in the source corresponds to it. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Nominatim lookup of OpenStreetMap node 1594641238 (place=village, name Tibberup, Helsingør Kommune, linked to Wikidata Q12343163) returns latitude 55.9831821 and longitude 12.5378199, rounded to [12.5378,55.9832]. Fryxell names Toberup, alias Tiberup, north of Humlebæk as the landing ground. A different Tibberup in Gribskov municipality is not used. The village node is a named-place sector reference about 1 km inland of the landing shore, not a surveyed beach position; no accuracy radius is claimed.
